observations.type: Native: title remains thick raised normal Korean, with clear counters and separate syllables. 720: title, English, descriptor, action fragments and long venue are all readable. 320: title and each action label remain recognizable; date is visible, venue naturally much smaller.
observations.space: Single continuous purple flow connects upper-left compression to middle-right pinch and lower rounded resting mass. Existing action fragments remain adjacent to their corresponding zones. Title is tight to the top/right edges without clipping. Date/venue retain a clear bottom area.
observations.material: Native: repaired ivory forms are clay sculptures with simplified same-color tips. Purple stretch striations, rounded masses and lower-right cast shadows still explain deformation. There are fine microtexture changes outside the hands, especially the upper purple pad and thin neck, but no new halo or torn boundary is visible.
observations.ai_slop: No arbitrary decoration, fake exhibition labels, extra glyphs, logo, or unrelated effect objects. The action sentence genuinely organizes the pressure/pull/rest image. Repair solves the mixed skin/clay logic; some dense modeling texture and tight title margin remain concrete finish limits.

repair_decision.reason: The observed material defect is sufficiently corrected while mandatory copy, clay3D energy and the assigned continuous action relation remain intact. No further actual mandatory defect identified.

residuals: Raised title fits close to the top/right edges, without current clipping.
The resting mound stays attached to the elongated neck; returning/recovery is conveyed by form and action copy rather than visible time progression.
Clay surfaces retain fairly dense modeling marks; the repair did not produce a perfectly smooth surface and no smoothness claim is made.
